answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a small refundable stake locked for a full epoch before it can earn. A hollow identity with no stake behind it gains nothing, while a mesa of real agents each carrying their own deposit makes mass creation expensive. Tying reputation to that stake, like a walnut that only cracks open after sustained honest work, means fake accounts cost more than they can extract, so attackers stop multiplying.
